note: Triennial election of Newry No. 2 (County Armagh) Rural District Council, twenty-nine single-member divisions, 1952. Nominations received by W. B. O'Donoghue on Tuesday 20 May 1952; contests in Bessbrook North, Camlough and Moybane, polled Thursday 5 June 1952. No nominations for Crossmaglen, Drumintee and Moyra Castle, whose sitting members were deemed re-elected. No party labels printed. Polled Thursday 5 June 1952. Clarke was the sitting member (1949). The County Armagh transcription published before 7 Nov 2026 (Newry Reporter, 12 June 1952, p. 8 ("Newry No. 2 R.D.C.")) read Peter Malachy Morris: 'Peter M. Morris'; Patrick Anthony McGeeney: 'Patrick McGeeney'; Thomas Clarke: 'Thomas Clarke'. Earlier transcription: The nominations print Morris's division as "Moybawn". Thomas Clarke: no party label printed in 1952. At other elections he stood as Anti-Partitionist (Moybane, 2 June 1949, printed 'Anti-Partitionist': Newry Telegraph, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Newry No. 2 (Co. Armagh) Rural District Council (election nominations)"); Frontier Sentinel, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Newry and Kilkeel Rural Councils' Nominations")) and as Nationalist (Crossmaglen, 5 June 1958, printed 'N.': Newry Telegraph, 7 June 1958, p. 4 ("Rural Council Elections"); Newry Telegraph, 24 May 1958, p. 1 ("The Council Elections: Newry No. 2 (Co. Armagh) Rural District Council (nominations)"); Newry Reporter, 12 June 1958, p. 2 ("The Rural Council Elections: most members retained seats", results with votes cast and spoilt)).
